newsitem.title: SUDAN: Tribal fighting resurfaces in western Sudan.
newsitem.headline: Tribal fighting resurfaces in western Sudan.

text.p: Fighting has broken out between two tribes in western Sudan less than a month after another two tribes signed a truce to end bloody clashes there, a newspaper reported on Thursday.
The privately-owned al-Rai al-Aam said there were fierce clashes and repeated attacks on villages in several areas in West Darfur state.
Gamar Hassan al-Tahir, a parliamentarian from the area, told the paper the current clashes were between the Masalit tribe and Arab tribes that had migrated from neighbouring Chad.
Tahir said some people had died in the clashes but did not say how many. He did not say why the tribes were fighting but did not rule out political and personal motives.
The parliamentarian did not say when the fighting broke out but said it had continued until Tuesday.
The governor of West Darfur was aware of the problem, which he blamed on lack of security supervision, Tahir told the paper.
Tahir said he would try to meet Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir to tell him about the clashes.
Representatives of the Zaghwa and Reizegat tribes signed a truce earlier this month after fighting that left between 60 and 100 people dead.
The tribes had fought over water and grazing rights and also accuse each other of armed robbery.
